rv.q: Golyak’s production achieves delicate balances between timeliness and timelessness, hilarity and horror, and the result is an astonishing piece of work.
Muscular performances and jaw-dropping design come together seamlessly for an evening of theater that will linger in my memory for a long time.

What Delirium gets right is capturing the lengths to which people will go to normalize the extreme, the rationalizations of people who've grown accustomed to untenable situations — whether domestic or political.

cn.t: Golyak's timely adaptation of Ionesco's absurdist comedy resonates with critics, who praise the leads' excellent chemistry as a bickering couple ignoring war outside their door. The production unlocks the 1963 play's relevance for today's world.
